_note: Mirrors the Monthly Concepts database in Notion (Creative Engine). Formats that creators cannot shoot themselves (AI UGC, Cartoon, AI-Musical) are left out on purpose.

formats.Talking Head: Creator speaks straight to camera. Hook is the first spoken line, said mid-thought as if the viewer walked in on it. One clear emotion on the face in second one.
formats.Yapper: Fast, unfiltered rant energy, often walking or in the car seat before driving. Hook is a blurted opinion or confession. Sentences are short and a little messy on purpose.
formats.Founder: The founder speaks in first person. Hook comes from the origin: the moment that made them build it, a mistake they made, or something they refuse to do. Calm, specific and credible. Never salesy, never 'hey guys'.
formats.Green Screen: Creator stands in front of a screenshot: a comment, a review, a listing, a text message. Hook reacts to what is on the screen, so the screenshot must be named in the visual.
formats.Unboxing: Hook sells curiosity about the package or the first impression. Open on the hands and the parcel, with an expectation that is about to be confirmed or broken.
formats.Table View: Top-down or across-the-table shot of hands and product. Hook is a visual demonstration or a side-by-side laid out on the table, with on-screen text doing the talking.
formats.Interview: Street or at-home interview feel, a question asked off camera. Hook is the question or a surprising first answer, cold open with no intro.
formats.Podcast: Two-mic conversation look. Hook is a quotable line lifted from the middle of a conversation, so it starts mid-sentence energy with no setup.
formats.Screen Recording: Notes app, text thread, search bar or comment section recorded on the phone. Hook is what is being typed or read, and it must be readable in under two seconds.
formats.No-Voiceover: No talking. Hook is on-screen text plus one strong visual action. Text is eight words or fewer and the action starts in the first second.
formats.Mashup: Quick cuts of several moments or several moms with a voiceover. Hook is a voiceover line that names the shared situation while the clips prove it is universal.

frameworks.PAS: Problem, agitate, solve. Hook names the problem in the viewer's own words. It never mentions the product.
frameworks.Comparison: This versus that. Hook sets up the two sides within the first three seconds and hints there is a clear winner, without naming a competitor brand.
frameworks.Testimonial: A lived experience. Hook is a specific moment from before the product, told in past tense, with a concrete detail (a place, a time, a number of minutes).
frameworks.Objection Handling: Hook voices the viewer's doubt out loud, ideally as something the creator believed too, then the video answers it.
frameworks.Transformation: Before and after. Hook shows or states the 'before' at its worst, or teases the contrast.
frameworks.Unique Mechanism: Why it works when other things did not. Hook teases the one design detail that changes things without explaining it yet.
frameworks.How It Works: Demonstration. Hook promises a quick show-me, often timed ('this takes ten seconds').
frameworks.Features & Benefits: Hook leads with the single most surprising benefit, not a list.
frameworks.Listicle: Hook promises a numbered list the viewer wants to finish, and the product is one natural item in it.
frameworks.Top 3: Hook promises three things, ranked or not, with the product as one of them.
frameworks.Top 5: Hook promises five things, with the product as one of them.
frameworks.Native: Looks like normal content, not an ad. Hook is a day-in-the-life or relatable moment. The product appears without being announced.
frameworks.Headline: One bold on-screen statement carries the ad. Hook is that headline, written like a news line or a meme caption.
frameworks.Offer: Hook leads with the deal or the guarantee. Only usable when the creator has been given an approved offer.

hook_patterns.Callout: Names the exact person it is for ('If your toddler...').
hook_patterns.Confession: Admits something slightly embarrassing or unpopular.
hook_patterns.Contrarian: Disagrees with common advice or a common purchase.
hook_patterns.Question they already ask: Says out loud the question the viewer has typed into a search bar.
hook_patterns.Mid-story cold open: Starts in the middle of a specific moment with no setup.
hook_patterns.Visual pattern interrupt: An unexpected action or framing in the first second, words come second.
hook_patterns.Mistake warning: Warns about something the creator got wrong first.
hook_patterns.Overheard: Quotes what someone else said (a stranger, partner, mother-in-law, the toddler).
hook_patterns.Timed dare: Promises to show something within a stated number of seconds.
hook_patterns.Number promise: Promises a specific count of things.
hook_patterns.Before and after tease: Shows the ending first or contrasts two states.
hook_patterns.Reaction to a comment: Replies to a real-sounding comment or review.
